lines: A snapped line once saved me from hauling in something worse than nothing.
Once the <wavy>fog</wavy> came in so thick I trusted the dock by smell.
An empty net can still bring home a lesson, though nobody cooks it.
There is a story from the dock, but it sounds smaller unless you were standing there.
Once a fish jumped into the boat and startled me more than I startled it.
A storm rolled in so fast the dock seemed to shrink under my feet.
I hauled up a boot once and three people claimed it was not theirs too quickly.
A child asked if fish gossip. I said only downstream.
The biggest catch I ever saw escaped because everyone tried to describe it at once.
I once followed a ripple and found a lost bucket instead of wisdom.
A foggy morning made the shore vanish and gave every sound a story.
There was a day when the river rose like it had remembered an old grudge.
A trader bragged about sea legs and slipped before reaching the dock.
I once fixed a net through rain while a fish watched like a supervisor.
The old boat creaks in three places and lies about which one matters.
A turtle blocked the landing for an hour and won the whole village's respect.
I saw moonlight on the river once and forgot every complaint I had saved.
One morning the fish bit so well nobody trusted it.
The river once returned a lost tool two weeks late and very smug.
